The level of service measurement is only made for signalized intersections, and then only when congestion has become noticeable enough to warrant investigation. A full description of the various level of service categories appears in Appendix B. Any intersection which is signalized but does not presently have a level of service designation is assumed to be functioning smoothly.
The following discussions of the specific traffic patters of each CNRA also lists the intersections which are currently on the City of San Jose's Transportation Division's priority list for signalization. Each discussion indicates the intersection location, its number on the priority list, and whether or not it is included in present plans for improvement. The final element of the traffic discussion is the traffic volumes on the neighborhood streets. These are given below for selected major streets in each CNRA for which data is available. As noted in the table, some traffic counts are not current.
Alma CNRA:
The Alma neighborhood is flanked on the east by Monterey Highway, a major arterial of six lanes and on the north by Alma Avenue, a major collector. The local neighborhood streets are based on a rectilinear grid system.
